media multitasking is not associated with distractibility in laboratory settings.
media multitasking does not impair performance on tests of distractor processing.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the relationship between media multitasking, as assessed with the media use questionnaire and cognitive control, is not as strong as initially suggested.
media multitasking does not seem to affect performance on distractor filtering tasks.
the association between media multitaskers and cognitive control is not as clear-cut as the original study suggests.
The main takeaway from our work is that
replication is important, even when the original findings have been published in prestigious journals.
